title: Signature Haven Wall Pendulum
body:
Specifications. Movement: Eight-day Signature wall movement. Pendulum length: 0.900 metres. Overall height: 86 cm. Chime and strike: Signature Haven chime. Case and dial materials: Signature warm oak case.

Mechanism. The pendulum governs timekeeping: its swing period follows T = 2π√(L/g) with g = 9.80665 m/s², so a pendulum of 0.900 metres sets the beat rate used by the escapement. The going train carries power from the weight drum or spring barrel through geared wheels to the escapement, which meters energy to the pendulum in small, regular steps and advances the hands. Weight-driven movements need a weekly wind for an eight-day run; the weights fall slowly and evenly, and a maintaining-power device keeps the pendulum swinging while the clock is wound.

Haven is the welcoming Signature wall clock, in warm oak with a soft chime made for entrance halls.

This is an original Signature design, created for this database and labeled signature-original. It is not presented as an authentic public or historical record.

Maintenance. Keep the clock level so the beat is even, with equal ticks on both swings. Wind on the same day each week, never forcing the key past its stop. Dust the case with a soft dry cloth, keep the movement dry and out of direct sun, and have the movement cleaned and oiled by a competent clock repairer every five to eight years. Never move a weight-driven clock with its weights hanging and its pendulum fitted.

Build and restoration guidance. Restoration starts with photographs and notes before anything is taken apart, then careful disassembly, cleaning, bushing of worn pivot holes, and reassembly in the reverse order. Replacement parts should match the original tooth counts and materials, and the finished movement is tested in beat before the dial and hands are refitted.

Tools. Clock key of the correct size, level, soft cloths, tweezers, screwdrivers sized for clock screws, oiler with clock oil, and a beat amplifier or a careful ear for beat setting.

print(f"Pendulum length: {L:.3f} m")
print(f"Period: {T:.4f} seconds")
print(f"Beat rate: {beats_per_hour:.1f} beats per hour")

title: Signature Crown Wall Pendulum
body:
Specifications. Movement: Eight-day Signature wall movement. Pendulum length: 0.900 metres. Overall height: 90 cm. Chime and strike: Signature Crown chime. Case and dial materials: Signature crowned mahogany case.

Mechanism. The pendulum governs timekeeping: its swing period follows T = 2π√(L/g) with g = 9.80665 m/s², so a pendulum of 0.900 metres sets the beat rate used by the escapement. The going train carries power from the weight drum or spring barrel through geared wheels to the escapement, which meters energy to the pendulum in small, regular steps and advances the hands. Weight-driven movements need a weekly wind for an eight-day run; the weights fall slowly and evenly, and a maintaining-power device keeps the pendulum swinging while the clock is wound.

Crown tops its wall case with a carved crest and gold chapter numerals, the flagship Signature wall pendulum clock.

This is an original Signature design, created for this database and labeled signature-original. It is not presented as an authentic public or historical record.

Maintenance. Keep the clock level so the beat is even, with equal ticks on both swings. Wind on the same day each week, never forcing the key past its stop. Dust the case with a soft dry cloth, keep the movement dry and out of direct sun, and have the movement cleaned and oiled by a competent clock repairer every five to eight years. Never move a weight-driven clock with its weights hanging and its pendulum fitted.

Build and restoration guidance. Restoration starts with photographs and notes before anything is taken apart, then careful disassembly, cleaning, bushing of worn pivot holes, and reassembly in the reverse order. Replacement parts should match the original tooth counts and materials, and the finished movement is tested in beat before the dial and hands are refitted.

Tools. Clock key of the correct size, level, soft cloths, tweezers, screwdrivers sized for clock screws, oiler with clock oil, and a beat amplifier or a careful ear for beat setting.
